cumbia-premiers-pas.title: Cumbia — first steps
cumbia-premiers-pas.description: From "I strum on the beats" to "I get people dancing". Each exercise works on just one difficulty at a time.

cumbia-01-pulsation.title: Feel the pulse
cumbia-01-pulsation.description: A single chord (C: just one finger, 3rd fret of the A string) and one downstroke on every beat. The goal isn't to sound pretty: it's to land EXACTLY with the kick drum and the click.
cumbia-01-pulsation.goal: Hold 2 loops in a row at 90 bpm without stopping.
tips: Tap your foot on every beat: your foot is your conductor.
Count out loud "1, 2, 3, 4". Yes, out loud, really.
If you get lost, don't stop: wait for the next "1" (the big orange dot) and jump back in.
Turn the guide ukulele off ("off" setting) once you feel comfortable: you'll hear better whether you're in time.

cumbia-02-contretemps.title: The off-beat, heart of cumbia
cumbia-02-contretemps.description: In cumbia, what makes people dance falls BETWEEN the beats. Here you only play the "&"s, with upstrokes. It feels strange at first: that's exactly what will put groove into your playing.
cumbia-02-contretemps.goal: Play the off-beats for 2 loops without slipping back onto the beats, at 90 bpm.
tips: Your hand moves non-stop like a windshield wiper: it goes DOWN without touching the strings on the beats, and comes back UP strumming on the "&"s.
Say "1 & 2 & 3 & 4 &", shouting the &s.
Tap your foot on the beats: your foot and your hand never hit at the same time.
Listen to the guiro: its "chk-chk" gives you all the little subdivisions.

cumbia-03-chucu.title: The "chucu-chucu" (chuck)
cumbia-03-chucu.description: Now we combine the two previous exercises: on the beats you CHUCK (the side or palm of your hand drops onto the strings: "chk"), and on the off-beats you strum up. The result: cumbia's famous "chucu-chucu" sound.
cumbia-03-chucu.goal: A nice dry chuck and a clear upstroke, 2 loops at 95 bpm.
tips: The chuck (✕): let your strumming hand fall flat onto the strings, like a little slap. There should be almost no note at all.
You can also mute with your fretting hand: just release the finger pressure at the moment of the ✕.
Keep the same continuous down-up motion as in the previous exercise: only the way you touch the strings changes.
Turn the metronome down and listen to the conga: it plays the same question-and-answer game.

cumbia-04-changement.title: First change: C ↔ G7
cumbia-04-changement.description: A very simple rhythm (4 downstrokes) so you can put all your attention on your fretting hand. The secret of an on-time change: you prepare it BEFORE you get there.
cumbia-04-changement.goal: Change with no gap and no delay, 2 loops at 85 bpm.
tips: Watch the "Next" box: when it lights up orange, your fingers should already be on their way.
On beat 4, let go of the chord a little early: an open string is better than being late on the 1.
The rhythm NEVER stops to wait for your fretting hand. If the chord isn't ready, strum anyway.
Practice the change silently, without strumming, 10 times in a row before starting the music.

cumbia-05-rasgueo.title: The cumbia rasgueo
cumbia-05-rasgueo.description: Before the rasgueo, the motion that carries it: your hand goes down-up without ever stopping, twice per beat, like a pendulum. Down on the beats (stronger), up on the "&"s (lighter). A single chord, C, so you only think about your strumming hand.
cumbia-05-rasgueo.goal: A steady pendulum, 2 loops at 100 bpm.
tips: The motion comes from a relaxed wrist, as if you were shaking water off your hand.
The downstroke is firm, the upstroke just brushes the high strings.
Tap your foot on the beats: your foot and the "down" land together.
This pendulum never stops in the next steps: some strokes will simply miss the strings on purpose.

cumbia-05-rasgueo~boum-boumta.title: "Boom, boom-ta"
cumbia-05-rasgueo~boum-boumta.description: The first half of the rasgueo, twice per bar: down on 1, then down-up on 2 and its "&". On the "&" of 1, your hand comes back up EMPTY, without touching the strings: it's the step 1 pendulum with one stroke missed on purpose.
cumbia-05-rasgueo~boum-boumta.goal: "Boom, boom-ta" right in time, 2 loops at 95 bpm.
tips: Sing "boom (empty) boom-ta, boom (empty) boom-ta".
Keep the pendulum going: for the empty upstroke, just move your hand slightly away from the strings.
If you stop during the gap, go back to step 1 for a few loops.

cumbia-05-rasgueo~trou-du-3.title: The gap on 3
cumbia-05-rasgueo~trou-du-3.description: The full pattern, still on a single chord. What's new: on 3, your hand goes down EMPTY (the "gap"), then strums on the way up on the "&" of 3, and ends with down-up on 4. That gap is what makes cumbia sway.
cumbia-05-rasgueo~trou-du-3.goal: The full pattern on C, 2 loops at 95 bpm.
tips: Sing "boom, boom-ta, (nothing) ta, boom-ta".
The upstroke after the gap often comes too early: really wait for the "&" of 3.
Compare with step 2: only the second half of the bar changes.

cumbia-05-rasgueo~silence.title: 🤫 Hold the pattern alone
cumbia-05-rasgueo~silence.description: The full pattern on C, but one bar in four the whole band stops (the guide ukulele too). Before adding chord changes, make sure the pattern holds up on its own.
cumbia-05-rasgueo~silence.goal: Land exactly with the band after every silence, 2 loops in a row.
tips: During the silence, sing the pattern out loud: "boom, boom-ta, (nothing) ta, boom-ta".
The gap on 3 is the trap: without the band, you tend to fill it in.

cumbia-05-rasgueo~demi-temps.title: Half a beat to change
cumbia-05-rasgueo~demi-temps.description: First chord change: C for two bars, then G7 for two bars. To help you, the very last "up" of the bar (the "&" of 4) is EMPTY: your strumming hand keeps its pendulum without touching the strings, and your fretting hand gets half a beat free to change chords.
cumbia-05-rasgueo~demi-temps.goal: The new chord ready right on the 1, 2 loops at 90 bpm.
tips: As soon as you've played the "down" on 4, let go of the chord and head for the next one.
Sing "boom, boom-ta, (nothing) ta, boom (change)".
C → G7: practise it without music first, 10 times in a row.

cumbia-05-rasgueo~deux-mesures.title: Change every 2 bars
cumbia-05-rasgueo~deux-mesures.description: The pattern gets its last "up" back: the full rasgueo, with a chord change every two bars. You get a whole bar to see the change coming.
cumbia-05-rasgueo~deux-mesures.goal: Change without breaking the pattern, 2 loops at 95 bpm.
tips: Change chords during the last "up" on 4: an open string ringing is no big deal.
Your strumming hand never stops to wait for your fretting hand.
If the change catches, go back to the previous step: the free half beat.

cumbia-05-rasgueo~chaque-mesure.title: Change every bar, with the half beat
cumbia-05-rasgueo~chaque-mesure.description: Now the chord changes on every bar: C, G7, C, G7… Twice as many changes, so the half-beat helper is back: the "&" of 4 is empty to let your fretting hand change.
cumbia-05-rasgueo~chaque-mesure.goal: A change on every bar with no delay on the 1, 2 loops at 90 bpm.
tips: Think "one chord ahead": while you play C, your fingers already know where G7 goes.
During the empty half beat, lift all your fingers and place the new chord in a single move.
If it's still hard, lower the tempo rather than stopping your strumming hand.

cumbia-05-rasgueo~complet.title: The full rasgueo
cumbia-05-rasgueo~complet.description: The "down, down-up, (miss), up, down-up" pattern with a change on every bar: the go-to strum of Latin and Caribbean music. It mixes beats and off-beats, which is what gives it its sway.
cumbia-05-rasgueo~complet.goal: The full pattern with the chord changes, 2 loops at 95 bpm.
tips: Your hand always goes down-up-down-up in eighth notes. The empty slots are MISSED strokes: your hand never stops.
Sing the pattern: "boom, boom-ta, (nothing), ta, boom-ta".
Start with the guide on "plays along", then switch to "fades after 2 loops".
To go further, turn on the "🤫 silence challenge" in the settings.

cumbia-06t-riff-grille.title: 🧪 Test: the notes inside the bar
cumbia-06t-riff-grille.description: Display trial. Each riff note has its own little fretboard right inside the bar, in its place: nothing jumps around, it's the lit-up step that moves forward. At the top, you get the band's chord diagrams back (Am then E7), which only change on each bar. Six notes, one per beat: A, C, G over Am, then G#, B, E over E7.
cumbia-06t-riff-grille.goal: All six notes without hesitating, 2 loops at 80 bpm.
tips: Read the bar ahead: the next note's fretboard is already shown next to the lit-up step.
The "next" box announces the move to E7: that's when your fretting hand changes position.
Beat 4 of each bar is empty: use it to place your finger for the next bar.

cumbia-06-riff.title: A cumbia riff
cumbia-06-riff.description: The riff fits in three notes per bar. First of all, we anchor the ones of the Am bar, one at a time: four times A0 (open A string), then four times A3 (A string, fret 3), then four times E3 (E string, fret 3). One note per beat, the same one for a whole bar: you have time to look at the fretboard, place your finger and listen to the sound. The "next" box lights up when it's time to change note.
cumbia-06-riff.goal: All three notes well placed, 2 loops at 60 bpm.
tips: No need to hold the chord with your fretting hand: the band plays Am.
A3 and E3 are both played with the ring finger, fret 3: only the string changes.
Pluck the string with your thumb, downward, without forcing.
Say the note name on every stroke: "A, A, A, A, C, C, C, C, G…".

cumbia-06-riff~notes-am.title: The Am notes, one per beat
cumbia-06-riff~notes-am.description: The three notes now follow each other within a single bar, one per beat: A, C, G, then beat 4 stays empty to get back to the start. The fretboard changes note on every beat.
cumbia-06-riff~notes-am.goal: A, C, G nice and even, 2 loops at 80 bpm.
tips: Keep your ring finger over fret 3: it moves from the A string to the E string without lifting high.
The empty beat is there to get back to the open A string.
Tap your foot: one note per step.

cumbia-06-riff~mesure-am.title: The Am bar in rhythm
cumbia-06-riff~mesure-am.description: Now the riff's rhythm, over A minor. Two extra A's are added: the notes land on 1, 2, the "&" of 2, the "&" of 3 and 4. The two middle notes fall BETWEEN the beats: that's where the riff swings.
cumbia-06-riff~mesure-am.goal: The Am bar right in time, 2 loops at 90 bpm.
tips: Sing the rhythm: "A . A-C . A G .".
Tap your foot on the beats: the C (A3) and the third A land as your foot comes up.
If a note slips away, go back to step 2 for a while.

cumbia-06-riff~ancrer-e7.title: Anchor the E7 notes
cumbia-06-riff~ancrer-e7.description: Second bar of the riff, same method: four times E4 (E string, fret 4, little finger), then four times A2 (A string, fret 2, middle finger), then four times E0 (open E string), over E7.
cumbia-06-riff~ancrer-e7.goal: All three notes well placed, 2 loops at 60 bpm.
tips: The little finger is the weakest: place it right behind the fret, on its tip.
During the four E4s, your middle finger is already waiting over fret 2.
Say the note name on every stroke: "G#, G#, G#, G#, B…".

cumbia-06-riff~notes-e7.title: The E7 notes, one per beat
cumbia-06-riff~notes-e7.description: The three E7 notes within a single bar, one per beat: G#, B, E, then beat 4 empty to get back to the start.
cumbia-06-riff~notes-e7.goal: G#, B, E nice and even, 2 loops at 80 bpm.
tips: Keep your little finger and middle finger hovering over their frets: only your plucking hand changes strings.
The empty beat is there to put your little finger back on E4.

cumbia-06-riff~mesure-e7.title: The E7 bar in rhythm
cumbia-06-riff~mesure-e7.description: The E7 bar on a loop, with the riff's rhythm. It's exactly the same rhythm as the Am bar: only the notes change.
cumbia-06-riff~mesure-e7.goal: The E7 bar right in time, 2 loops at 90 bpm.
tips: Same rhythm as the Am bar: "G# . G#-B . G# E .".
Keep both your little finger and middle finger ready.
The final E0 leads back to the start: link it with no gap.

cumbia-06-riff~enchainer.title: Linking Am and E7, one note per beat
cumbia-06-riff~enchainer.description: All six notes in a row, one per beat, without the rhythm: what's new is moving from one bar to the next. Beat 4 of each bar is empty: use it to put your finger on the first note of the next bar ("next" box).
cumbia-06-riff~enchainer.goal: All six notes without hesitating, 2 loops at 80 bpm.
tips: During the empty beat after the G (E3), your little finger is already heading for E4.
Read the tab in "The whole loop": each line is a string (A at the top), the number is the fret.
Say: "A, C, G, (place) G#, B, E, (place)".

cumbia-06-riff~complet.title: The full riff
cumbia-06-riff~complet.description: Putting it all together: the rhythm of the Am and E7 bars, and moving from one to the other without stopping. The riff follows the chords: A minor, then E7.
cumbia-06-riff~complet.goal: The riff with no hesitation, 2 loops at 90 bpm.
tips: Colors = strings: pink = A, yellow = E, turquoise = C, orange = G.
Play with your thumb or index finger — always the same strumming-hand finger to start with.
Repeated notes should be perfectly even: that's what sounds "cumbia".
Stuck on one bar? Click it in "The whole loop" to practise it on its own.
Once you're comfortable, turn the guide off: the band plays Am then E7, and your riff has to stand on its own.

cumbia-07-mineur.title: Cumbia in A minor
cumbia-07-mineur.description: Lots of cumbias are in a minor key. Four chords, the "chucu-chucu", and the E7 that always leads back to A minor.
cumbia-07-mineur.goal: All 4 chords in chucu-chucu, 2 loops at 95 bpm.
tips: Am → Dm: add two fingers; the one on the G string stays put.
Dm → E7: this is the tricky change, so practice it on its own first, without music.
During the chuck (✕), your fretting hand can relax: use that moment to change chords!

cumbia-08-silence.title: Keep it going alone: the silence challenge
cumbia-08-silence.description: One bar in four, everyone goes quiet (even the metronome and the lit-up step). Keep playing and counting: when the band comes back, you must be right on the "1". This is THE test that shows whether the rhythm is really inside you.
cumbia-08-silence.goal: Land back in time after every silence, 4 loops at 100 bpm.
tips: During the silence, count out loud and tap your foot harder.
If you're early when the band comes back, you speed up when you're on your own (very common!).
The guide fades after 2 loops: from then on, you're the band's ukulele.

cumbia-09-vitesse.title: Up to real tempo
cumbia-09-vitesse.description: The "Andalusian" progression Am – G – F – E7, everywhere in cumbia, with the full rasgueo. We build up to the tempo of a real dance-hall cumbia.
cumbia-09-vitesse.goal: Hold 2 loops at 110 bpm, guide off.
tips: Use "🐢 Too fast!" without shame: the app slows back down and gives you more time.
The faster it gets, the more relaxed your strumming hand must be: the motion comes from the wrist, not the arm.
Your record is saved: come back tomorrow and you'll go faster (your brain consolidates while you sleep).

cumbia-02-contretemps~essuie-glace.title: Remedy: the windshield wiper you can hear
cumbia-02-contretemps~essuie-glace.description: If the off-beat keeps slipping away, make your motion audible: the hand brushes the strings on the way down on the beats (very softly) and strums clearly on the way up on the "&"s. The down is your landmark, the up makes the music.
cumbia-02-contretemps~essuie-glace.goal: An almost silent down, a crisp up, 2 loops at 80 bpm.
tips: The down is just a brush: barely one or two strings.
Think "soft / LOUD / soft / LOUD".
Once it's steady, go down further and further from the strings: you're back to the original exercise.

cumbia-02-contretemps~ancre.title: Anchored on the 1
cumbia-02-contretemps~ancre.description: A single downstroke on the 1, so you know where you are, then off-beats only. The 1 is your foothold: the rest of the bar is played "in between".
cumbia-02-contretemps~ancre.goal: Keep a solid 1 and three steady "&"s, 2 loops at 85 bpm.
tips: Say "ONE and (2) and (3) and (4) and": only the words you say out loud are played.
The downstroke on the 1 and the following up make a round trip: don't stop after the 1.
Listen to the kick drum: it lands with your downstroke.

cumbia-02-contretemps~seul.title: The guide leaves you alone
cumbia-02-contretemps~seul.description: The guide ukulele plays two loops and then goes quiet: nobody plays your off-beats for you anymore. Only the band remains, playing ON the beats. Your job is to stay in between.
cumbia-02-contretemps~seul.goal: 4 loops without the guide, never slipping onto the beats, at 90 bpm.
tips: Tap your foot: your foot lands with the kick drum, your hand never does.
If you find yourself on the beats, stop for one bar, listen to the guiro, and come back in on an "&".

cumbia-02-contretemps~sans-guiro.title: Without the guiro
cumbia-02-contretemps~sans-guiro.description: The guiro was giving you every subdivision. We cut it: only the bass and the kick drum on 1 and 3 remain. The "&"s now exist only in your head… and in your hand.
cumbia-02-contretemps~sans-guiro.goal: Steady off-beats without the guiro, 2 loops at 90 bpm.
tips: Hum the guiro's "chk-chk" while you play.
Click "guiro" in the band to bring it back if needed, then cut it again.

cumbia-02-contretemps~silence.title: 🤫 Silence challenge
cumbia-02-contretemps~silence.description: One bar in four, everything stops. The real off-beat test: keep playing BETWEEN beats that nobody marks anymore, and land right when the band comes back.
cumbia-02-contretemps~silence.goal: Land on the right "&" after every silence, 2 loops in a row.
tips: During the silence, count louder and keep your foot on the beats.
Your hand keeps swinging up and down in the air: it's what keeps the tempo.

cumbia-02-contretemps~changement.title: Off-beats and a chord change
cumbia-02-contretemps~changement.description: The off-beat has a hidden gift: on the 1, your strumming hand passes in the air… the perfect moment to change chords. C and G7 alternate every bar.
cumbia-02-contretemps~changement.goal: Change chords during the empty beat, without being late on the first "&", 2 loops at 85 bpm.
tips: Change chords while the hand goes down in the air on the 1: you have half a beat to spare.
If the first "&" of the bar slips, no big deal: catch the next one.

cumbia-02-contretemps~tempo-bal.title: Towards dance-hall tempo
cumbia-02-contretemps~tempo-bal.description: Real cumbia is danced around 100 bpm and up. The faster it gets, the smaller and looser the motion must be: the wrist does the work, not the arm.
tips: Make the motion smaller: the hand hardly moves away from the strings.
If you tense up, press "Too fast!": you'll stay longer at the previous tempo.

cumbia-04-changement~deux-mesures.title: More time: 2 bars per chord
cumbia-04-changement~deux-mesures.description: To start gently: each chord lasts two bars. You have plenty of time to see the change coming in the "next" box.
cumbia-04-changement~deux-mesures.goal: Change right on the 1, 2 loops at 85 bpm.

cumbia-04-changement~trois-accords.title: A third chord: F
cumbia-04-changement~trois-accords.description: We add a bar of F to the loop: C – F – C – G7. F takes two fingers (G string fret 2, E string fret 1): get it ready during the C bar.
cumbia-04-changement~trois-accords.goal: All three chords with no gaps, 2 loops at 80 bpm.
tips: From C to F: lift the C finger and place both F fingers at once, in a single move.
Practise C → F → C → G7 silently, without strumming, before starting the music.

cumbia-04-changement~cadence.title: The full cadence: C – F – G7 – C
cumbia-04-changement~cadence.description: The most played chord sequence in popular music. This time F and G7 follow each other directly: two changes in a row.
cumbia-04-changement~cadence.goal: The whole cadence on time, 2 loops at 85 bpm.
tips: From F to G7, the finger on the E string (fret 1) stays put: keep it down and pivot the others around it.
Look one chord ahead: while you play F, already think G7.

cumbia-04-changement~main-qui-bouge.title: Change without stopping the hand
cumbia-04-changement~main-qui-bouge.description: Same cadence, but now the strumming hand swings in eighth notes (strong down, light up). It never stops, even during the change: the fretting hand has to keep up.
cumbia-04-changement~main-qui-bouge.goal: A continuous swing through the changes, 2 loops at 85 bpm.
tips: The last "&" before the change may ring open (open strings): that's normal and barely noticeable.
Never slow the strumming hand to wait for the fretting hand.

cumbia-04-changement~silence.title: 🤫 Silence challenge
cumbia-04-changement~silence.description: The C – F – G7 – C cadence, and one bar in four the band goes quiet. During the silence you play alone… and that's exactly where the return to C happens: place it with no help.
cumbia-04-changement~silence.goal: Land with the band on the right chord after every silence, 2 loops in a row.

cumbia-01-pulsation~silence.title: 🤫 Silence challenge
cumbia-01-pulsation~silence.description: Same rhythm, but one bar in four the whole band stops (the guide ukulele too). Keep going alone, counting out loud, and land right on the 1 when the music comes back.
cumbia-01-pulsation~silence.goal: Land exactly with the band after every silence, 2 loops in a row.

cumbia-03-chucu~silence.title: 🤫 Silence challenge
cumbia-03-chucu~silence.description: Same rhythm, but one bar in four the whole band stops (the guide ukulele too). Keep going alone, counting out loud, and land right on the 1 when the music comes back.
cumbia-03-chucu~silence.goal: Land exactly with the band after every silence, 2 loops in a row.
